(for example “disclose:yi na +v -g o”) The example sets [b]inventory[/b] to [i]prompt[/i] and default to [i]yes[/i], [b]attributes[/b] to [i]prompt[/i] and default to [i]no[/i], [b]vanquished[/b] to [i]disclose without prompting[/i], [b]genocided[/b] to [i]not disclose[/i] and [i]not prompt[/i], [b]conduct[/b] to implicitly [i]prompt[/i] and default to [i]no[/i], and [b]overview[/b] to [i]disclose without prompting[/i].

Note that the vanquished monsters list includes all monsters killed by traps and each other as well as by you. And the dungeon overview shows all levels you had visited but does not reveal things about them that you hadn't discovered.
[b]dogname[/b] — Name your starting dog (for example “dogname:Fang”). Cannot be set with the ‘[code]O[/code]’ command.

[b]extmenu[/b] — Changes the extended commands interface to pop-up a menu of available commands. It is keystroke compatible with the traditional interface except that it does not require that you hit [i]Enter[/i]. It is implemented for the tty interface (default off).

For the X11 interface, which always uses a menu for choosing an extended command, it controls whether the menu shows all available commands (on) or just the subset of commands which have traditionally been considered extended ones (off).
[b]female[/b] — An obsolete synonym for “[code]gender:female[/code]”. Cannot be set with the ‘[code]O[/code]’ command.

[b]fireassist[/b] — This option controls what happens when you attempt the ‘f’ (fire) and don't have an appropriate launcher, such as a bow or a sling, wielded. If on, you will automatically wield the launcher. Default is on.
[b]fixinv[/b] — An object's inventory letter sticks to it when it's dropped (default on). If this is off, dropping an object shifts all the remaining inventory letters. Persistent.
[b]force_invmenu[/b] — Commands asking for an inventory item show a menu instead of a text query with possible menu letters. Default is off.

[b]fruit[/b] — Name a fruit after something you enjoy eating (for example “fruit:mango”) (default “slime mold”). Basically a nostalgic whimsy that NetHack uses from time to time. You should set this to something you find more appetizing than slime mold. Apples, oranges, pears, bananas, and melons already exist in NetHack, so don't use those.

[b]gender[/b] — Your starting gender ([code]gender:male[/code] or [code]gender:female[/code]). You may specify just the first letter. Although you can still denote your gender using either of the deprecated [i]male[/i] and [i]female[/i] options, if the [i]gender[/i] option is also present it will take precedence. See [i]role[/i] for a description of how to use negation to exclude choices.

If [code]gender[/code] is not specified, there is no default value; player will be prompted unless role and/or race forces a choice for gender. Cannot be set with the ‘[code]O[/code]’ command. Persistent.

[b]goldX[/b] — When filtering objects based on bless/curse state (BUCX), whether to treat gold pieces as X (unknown bless/curse state, when “on”) or U (known to be uncursed, when “off”, the default). Gold is never blessed or cursed, but it is not described as “uncursed” even when the [i]implicit_uncursed[/i] option is “off”.

[b]help[/b] — If more information is available for an object looked at with the ‘/’ command, ask if you want to see it (default on). Turning help off makes just looking at things faster, since you aren't interrupted with the “More info?” prompt, but it also means that you might miss some interesting and/or important information. Persistent.

[b]herecmd_menu[/b] — When using a windowport that supports mouse and clicking on yourself or next to you, show a menu of possible actions for the location. Same as “#herecmdmenu” and “#therecmdmenu” commands.

[b]hilite_pet[/b] — Visually distinguish pets from similar animals (default off). The behavior of this option depends on the type of windowing you use. In text windowing, text highlighting or inverse video is often used; with tiles, generally displays a heart symbol near pets.
With the tty or curses interface, the [i]petattr[/i] option controls how to highlight pets and setting it will turn the [i]hilite_pet[/i] option on or off as warranted.

[b]hilite_pile[/b] — Visually distinguish piles of objects from individual objects (default off). The behavior of this option depends on the type of windowing you use. In text windowing, text highlighting or inverse video is often used; with tiles, generally displays a small plus-symbol beside the object on the top of the pile.
[b]hitpointbar[/b] — Show a hit point bar graph behind your name and title in the status display (default off).

The “curses” interface supports it even if the status highlighting feature has been disabled when building the program. The “tty” and “mswin” (aka “Windows GUI”) interfaces support it only if status highlighting is left enabled when building. You don't need to set up any highlighting rules in order to display the bar. If there is one for hitpoints in effect and it specifies color, that color will be used for the bar. However if it specifies video attributes, they will be ignored in favor of [i]inverse[/i]. For tty and curses, [i]blink[/i] will also be used if the current hitpoint value is at or below the [i]critical HP[/i] threshold.

The “Qt” interface also supports hitpointbar, by drawing a solid bar above the name and title with a hard-coded color scheme. (As of this writing, having the bar enabled unintentionally inhibits resizing the status panel. To resize that, use the [code]#optionsfull[/code] command to toggle the [i]hitpointbar[/i] option off, perform the resize while it's off, then use the same command to toggle it back on.)
[b]horsename[/b] — Name your starting horse (for example “horsename:Trigger”). Cannot be set with the ‘[code]O[/code]’ command.
[b]ignintr[/b] — Ignore interrupt signals, including breaks (default off). Persistent.
[b]implicit_uncursed[/b] — Omit “uncursed” from object descriptions when it can be deduced from other aspects of the description (default on). Persistent.
If you use menu coloring, you may want to turn this off.
[b]legacy[/b] — Display an introductory message when starting the game (default on). Persistent.
[b]lit_corridor[/b] — Show corridor squares seen by night vision or a light source held by your character as lit (default off). Persistent.
[b]lootabc[/b] — When using a menu to interact with a container, use the old ‘a’, ‘b’, and ‘c’ keyboard shortcuts rather than the mnemonics ‘o’, ‘i’, and ‘b’ (default off). Persistent.
[b]mail[/b] — Enable mail delivery during the game (default on). Persistent.
[b]male[/b] — An obsolete synonym for “[code]gender:male[/code]”. Cannot be set with the ‘[code]O[/code]’ command.

[b]mention_decor[/b] — Give feedback when walking onto various dungeon features such as stairs, fountains, or altars which are ordinarily only described when covered by one or more objects (default off). Cannot be set with the ‘[code]O[/code]’ command. Persistent.
[b]mention_map[/b] — Give feedback when interesting map locations change (default off).
[b]mention_walls[/b] — Give feedback when walking against a wall (default off). Persistent.
[b]menucolors[/b] — Enable coloring menu lines (default off). See “Configuring Menu Colors” on how to configure the colors.

[b]menustyle[/b] — Controls the method used when you need to choose various objects (in response to the [code]Drop[/code] (aka [code]droptype[/code]) command, for instance). The value specified should be the first letter of one of the following: traditional, combination, full, or partial. Default is [code]full[/code]. Persistent.

Traditional was the only method available for very early versions; it consists of a prompt for object class characters, followed by an object-by-object prompt for all items matching the selected object class(es). Combination starts with a prompt for object class(es) of interest, but then displays a menu of matching objects rather than prompting one-by-one. Full displays a menu of object classes rather than a character prompt, and then a menu of matching objects for selection. (Choosing its ‘A’ (Autoselect-All) choice skips the second menu. To avoid choosing that by accident, set [code]paranoid_confirm:AutoAll[/code] to require confirmation.) Partial skips the object class filtering and immediately displays a menu of all objects.
[b]menu_deselect_all[/b] — Key to deselect all items in a menu. Default ‘-’.
[b]menu_deselect_page[/b] — Key to deselect all items on this page of a menu. Default ‘\’.
[b]menu_first_page[/b] — Key to jump to the first page in a menu. Default ‘^’.

[b]menu_headings[/b] — Controls how the headings in a menu are highlighted. Takes a text attribute, or text color and attribute separated by ampersand. For allowed attributes and colors, see “Configuring Menu Colors”. Not all ports can actually display all types.
[b]menu_invert_all[/b] — Key to invert all items in a menu. Default ‘@’.
[b]menu_invert_page[/b] — Key to invert all items on this page of a menu. Default ‘~’.
[b]menu_last_page[/b] — Key to jump to the last page in a menu. Default ‘|’.
[b]menu_next_page[/b] — Key to go to the next menu page. Default ‘>’.

[b]menu_objsyms[/b] — Inventory and other object menus are normally separated by object class (weapons, armor, and so forth), with a menu header line at the beginning of each group. You can have menus add the display symbol for the class of objects for each header line. You can also add the display symbol for the individual item in each menu entry. For a tiles map, that would be a small rendition of an object's tile. For a text map, it is the same character as is used for the object's class, which would be most useful when there are no headers separating objects among classes. Possible values are
[indent][b]0 - None[/b] — no symbols for either header lines or menu entries;[/indent]
[indent][b]1 - Headers[/b] — show symbols on header lines but not entries;[/indent]
[indent][b]2 - Entries[/b] — show symbols on menu entry lines but not headers;[/indent]
[indent][b]3 - Both[/b] — show symbols on headers and entries;[/indent]
[indent][b]4 - Conditional[/b] — only show symbols for entries if there are no headers;[/indent]
[indent][b]5 - One-or-other[/b] — show symbols on headers, or on entries if no headers.[/indent]
Supported by tty and curses. When setting the value, it can be specified by digit or keyword. The default value is [code]Conditional[/code] (4).
[b]menu_overlay[/b] — Do not clear the screen before drawing menus, and align menus to the right edge of the screen. Only for the tty port. (default on)
[b]menu_previous_page[/b] — Key to go to the previous menu page. Default ‘<’.
[b]menu_search[/b] — Key to search for some text and toggle selection state of matching menu items. Default ‘:’.
[b]menu_select_all[/b] — Key to select all items in a menu. Default ‘.’.
[b]menu_select_page[/b] — Key to select all items on this page of a menu. Default ‘,’.
[b]menu_shift_left[/b] — Key to scroll a menu—one which has been scrolled right—back to the left. Implemented for [i]perm_invent[/i] only by curses and X11. Default ‘{’.
[b]menu_shift_right[/b] — Key to scroll a menu which has text beyond the right edge to the right. Implemented for [i]perm_invent[/i] only by curses and X11. Default ‘}’.
[b]mon_movement[/b] — Show a message when hero notices a monster movement (default is off).
[b]monpolycontrol[/b] — Prompt for new form whenever any monster changes shape (default off). Debug mode only.
[b]montelecontrol[/b] — Prompt for destination whenever any monster gets teleported (default off). Debug mode only.
[b]mouse_support[/b] — Allow use of the mouse for input and travel. Valid settings are:
Omitting a value is the same as specifying 1 and negating [i]mouse_support[/i] is the same as specifying 0.
[b]msghistory[/b] — The number of top line messages to keep (and be able to recall with ‘^P’) (default 20). Cannot be set with the ‘[code]O[/code]’ command.

[b]msg_window[/b] — Allows you to change the way recalled messages are displayed. Currently it is only supported for tty (all four choices) and for curses (‘[code]f[/code]’ and ‘[code]r[/code]’ choices, default ‘[code]r[/code]’). The possible values are:
For backward compatibility, no value needs to be specified (which defaults to “full”), or it can be negated (which defaults to “single”).

[b]name[/b] — Set your character's name (defaults to your user name). You can also set your character's role by appending a dash and one or more letters of the role (that is, by suffixing one of [i]-A -B -C -H -K -M -P -Ra -Ro -S -T -V -W[/i]). If [i]-@[/i] is used for the role, then a random one will be automatically chosen.

On some systems, the default is the player's user name; on others, there is no default and the player will be prompted. The former can made to behave like the latter by specifying a generic name such as ``player''. Cannot be set with the ‘[code]O[/code]’ command.
[b]news[/b] — Read the NetHack news file, if present (default on). Since the news is shown at the beginning of the game, there's no point in setting this with the ‘O’ command.
[b]nudist[/b] — Start the character with no armor (default false). Persistent.
[b]null[/b] — Send padding nulls to the terminal (default on). Persistent.
[b]number_pad[/b] — Use digit keys instead of letters to move (default 0 or off). Valid settings are:
[indent][b] 0[/b] — move by letters; “[code]yuhjklbn[/code]”[/indent]
[indent][b] 1[/b] — move by numbers; digit ‘5’ acts as ‘G’ movement prefix[/indent]
[indent][b] 2[/b] — like 1 but ‘5’ works as ‘g’ prefix instead of as ‘G’[/indent]
[indent][b] 3[/b] — by numbers using phone key layout; 123 above, 789 below[/indent]
[indent][b] 4[/b] — combines 3 with 2; phone layout plus MS-DOS compatibility[/indent]
[indent][b]-1[/b] — by letters but use ‘z’ to go northwest, ‘y’ to zap wands[/indent]

For backward compatibility, omitting a value is the same as specifying 1 and negating [i]number_pad[/i] is the same as specifying 0. (Settings 2 and 4 are for compatibility with MS-DOS or old PC Hack; in addition to the different behavior for ‘5’, ‘Alt-5’ acts as ‘G’ and ‘Alt-0’ acts as ‘I’. Setting -1 is to accommodate some QWERTZ keyboards which have the location of the ‘y’ and ‘z’ keys swapped.) When moving by numbers, to enter a count prefix for those commands which accept one (such as “12s” to search twelve times), precede it with the letter ‘n’ (“n12s”).

[b]packorder[/b] — Specify the order to list object types in (default “")[lb]%?+!=/(*`0_”). The value of this option should be a string containing the symbols for the various object types. Any omitted types are filled in at the end from the previous order.
[b]paranoid_confirmation[/b] — A space separated list of specific situations where alternate prompting is desired. The default is “paranoid_confirmation:pray swim trap”.

[indent][b]Confirm[/b] — for any prompts which are set to require “yes” rather than ‘y’, also require “no” to reject instead of accepting any non-yes response as no; changes pray and AutoAll to require “yes” or ‘no’ too;[/indent]
[indent][b]quit[/b] — require “yes” rather than ‘y’ to confirm quitting the game or switching into non-scoring explore mode;[/indent]
[indent][b]die[/b] — require “yes” rather than ‘y’ to confirm dying (not useful in normal play; applies to explore mode);[/indent]
[indent][b]bones[/b] — require “yes” rather than ‘y’ to confirm saving bones data when dying in debug mode;[/indent]
[indent][b]attack[/b] — require “yes” rather than ‘y’ to confirm attacking a peaceful monster;[/indent]
[indent][b]wand-break[/b] — require “yes” rather than ‘y’ to confirm breaking a wand with the [code]apply[/code] command;[/indent]
[indent][b]eating[/b] — require “yes” rather than ‘y’ to confirm whether to continue eating;[/indent]
[indent][b]Were-change[/b] — require “yes” rather than ‘y’ to confirm changing form due to lycanthropy when hero has polymorph control;[/indent]
[indent][b]pray[/b] — require ‘y’ to confirm an attempt to pray rather than immediately praying; on by default; (to require “yes” rather than just ‘y’, set Confirm too);[/indent]

[indent][b]trap[/b] — require ‘y’ to confirm an attempt to move into or onto a known trap, unless doing so is considered to be harmless; when enabled, this confirmation is also used for moving into visible gas cloud regions; (to require “yes” rather than just ‘y’, set Confirm too); confirmation can be skipped by using the ‘[code]m[/code]’ movement prefix;[/indent]

[indent][b]swim[/b] — prevent walking into water or lava; on by default; (to deliberately step onto/into such terrain when this is set, use the ‘[code]m[/code]’ movement prefix when adjacent);[/indent]

[indent][b]AutoAll[/b] — require confirmation when the ‘A’ (Autoselect-All) choice is selected in object class filtering menus for [code]menustyle:Full[/code]; (to require “yes” rather than just ‘y’, set Confirm too);[/indent]
[indent][b]Remove[/b] — require selection from inventory for ‘R’ and ‘T’ commands even when wearing just one applicable item;[/indent]
[indent][b]all[/b] — turn on all of the above.[/indent]

By default, the pray, swim, and trap choices are enabled, the others disabled. To disable them without setting any of the other choices, use [code]paranoid_confirmation:none[/code]. To keep them enabled while setting any of the others, you can include them in the new list, such as [code]paranoid_confirmation:attack pray swim Remove[/code] or you can precede the first entry in the list with a plus sign, [code]paranoid_confirmation:+attack Remove[/code]. To remove an entry that has been previously set without removing others, precede the first entry in the list with a minus sign, [code]paranoid_confirmation:-swim[/code]. To both add some new entries and remove some old ones, you can use multiple [i]paranoid_confirmation[/i] option settings, or you can use the ‘[code]+[/code]’ form and list entries to be added by their name and entries to be removed by ‘[code]![/code]’ and name. The positive (no ‘!’) and negative (with ‘!’) entries can be intermixed.
[b]pauper[/b] — Start the character with no possessions (default false). Persistent.
Also start with no spells or skills, which are tied to starting equipment. Does not inhibit acquiring and using items, spells, and skills once play has started.
[b]perm_invent[/b] — If true, always display your current inventory in a window (default false).

This only makes sense for windowing system interfaces that implement this feature. For those that do, the [i]perminv_mode[/i] option can be used to refine what gets displayed for [i]perm_invent[/i]. Setting that to a value other than [i]none[/i] while [i]perm_invent[/i] is false will change it to true.
[b]perminv_mode[/b] — Augments the [i]perm_invent[/i] option. Value is one of
[indent][b][code]none[/code][/b] — behave as if [i]perm_invent[/i] is false;[/indent]
[indent][b][code]all[/code][/b] — show all inventory except for gold;[/indent]
[indent][b][code]full[/code][/b] — show full inventory including gold;[/indent]
[indent][b][code]in-use[/code][/b] — only show items which are in use (worn, wielded, lit lamp).[/indent]
Default is [i]none[/i] but if [i]perm_invent[/i] gets set to true while it is [i]none[/i] it will be changed to [i]all[/i].
Note: if gold has been equipped in quiver/ammo-pouch then it will be included for [i]all[/i] despite that mode normally omitting gold.

[b]petattr[/b] — Specifies one or more text highlighting attributes to use when showing pets on the map. Effectively a superset of the [i]hilite_pet[/i] boolean option. Curses or tty interface only; value is one of none, bold, dim, underline, italic, blink, and inverse. Some of those choices might not work, depending upon terminal hardware or terminal emulation software.

[b]pettype[/b] — Specify the type of your initial pet, if you are playing a character class that uses multiple types of pets; or choose to have no initial pet at all. Possible values are “cat”, “dog”, “horse”, and “none”. If the choice is not allowed for the role you are currently playing, it will be silently ignored. For example, “horse” will only be honored when playing a knight. Cannot be set with the ‘[code]O[/code]’ command.

[b]pickup_burden[/b] — When you pick up an item that would exceed this encumbrance level (Unencumbered, Burdened, streSsed, straiNed, overTaxed, or overLoaded), you will be asked if you want to continue. (Default ‘S’). Persistent.

[b]pickup_stolen[/b] — If this option is on and [i]autopickup[/i] is also on, try to pick up things that a monster stole from you, even if they aren't in [i]pickup_types[/i] or match an autopickup exception. Default is on. Persistent.

[b]pickup_thrown[/b] — If this option is on and [i]autopickup[/i] is also on, try to pick up things that you threw, even if they aren't in [i]pickup_types[/i] or match an autopickup exception. Default is on. Persistent.
[b]pickup_types[/b] — Specify the object types to be picked up when [i]autopickup[/i] is on. Default is all types. Persistent.

The value is a list of object symbols, such as [code]pickup_types:$?![/code] to pick up gold, scrolls, and potions. You can use [i]autopickup_exception[/i] configuration file lines to further refine [code]autopickup[/code] behavior.

There is no way to set [code]pickup_types[/code] to “[i]none[/i]”. (Setting it to an empty value reverts to “[i]all[/i]”.) If you want to avoid automatically picking up any types of items but do want to have [code]autopickup[/code] on in order to have [code]autopickup_exception[/code] settings control what you do and don't pick up, you can set [code]pickup_types[/code] to ‘[code].[/code]’. That is the type symbol for [i]venom[/i] and you won't come across any venom items so won't unintentionally pick such up.

[b]pile_limit[/b] — When walking across a pile of objects on the floor, threshold at which the message “there are few/several/many objects here” is given instead of showing a popup list of those objects. A value of 0 means “no limit” (always list the objects); a value of 1 effectively means “never show the objects” since the pile size will always be at least that big; default value is 5. Persistent.

[b]playmode[/b] — Values are “normal”, “explore”, or “debug”. Allows selection of explore mode (also known as discovery mode) or debug mode (also known as wizard mode) instead of normal play. Debug mode might only be allowed for someone logged in under a particular user name (on multi-user systems) or specifying a particular character name (on single-user systems) or it might be disabled entirely. Requesting it when not allowed or not possible results in explore mode instead. Default is normal play.

[b]price_quotes[/b] — Whenever the game mentions the name of an object you haven't identified yet, it also mentions the range of buy and sell prices you have seen for that item (to help narrow down what it could be). The price shown is the unit price for one item (even when you are looking at a stack of multiple items). Many players may want to turn this on while identifying objects, and then turn it back off again for general play. Default is off.

[b]pushweapon[/b] — Using the ‘w’ (wield) command when already wielding something pushes the old item into your alternate weapon slot (default off). Likewise for the ‘a’ (apply) command if it causes the applied item to become wielded. Persistent.
[b]query_menu[/b] — Use a menu when asked specific yes/no queries, instead of a prompt.

[b]quick_farsight[/b] — When set, usually prevents the “you sense your surroundings” message where play pauses to allow you to browse the map whenever clairvoyance randomly activates. Some situations, such as being underwater or engulfed, ignore this option. It does not affect the clairvoyance spell where pausing to examine revealed objects or monsters is less intrusive. Default is off. Persistent.

[b]race[/b] — Selects your race (for example, [code]race:human[/code]). Choices are [code]human[/code], [code]dwarf[/code], [code]elf[/code], [code]gnome[/code], and [code]orc[/code] but most roles restrict which of the non-human races are allowed. See [i]role[/i] for a description of how to use negation to exclude choices.
If [code]race[/code] is not specified, there is no default value; player will be prompted unless role forces a choice for race. Cannot be set with the ‘[code]O[/code]’ command. Persistent.
[b]reroll[/b] — Allows rerolling your character's starting inventory and attributes (default false). Persistent.

Note that rerolling your character is not a recommended way to play if aiming merely to win (a lucky start has a much smaller influence on whether or not you win the game than your actions later in the game). This option exists partly as an acknowledgement that some players will insist on doing so anyway, and partly because rerolling may be necessary for certain types of challenge games.
[b]rest_on_space[/b] — Make the space bar a synonym for the ‘.’ (#wait) command (default off). Persistent.
[b]role[/b] — Pick your type of character (for example, [code]role:Samurai[/code]); synonym for [i]character.[/i] See [i]name[/i] for an alternate method of specifying your role.

This option can also be used to limit selection when role is chosen randomly. Use a space-separated list of roles and either negate each one or negate the option itself instead. Negation is accomplished in the same manner as with [i]boolean options[/i], by prefixing the option or its value(s) with ‘!’ or “no”.
Examples:

[code]OPTIONS=role:!arc !bar !kni
OPTIONS=!role:arc bar kni[/code]
There can be multiple instances of the [i]role[/i] option if they're all negations.
If [code]role[/code] is not specified, there is no default value; player will be prompted. Cannot be set with the ‘[code]O[/code]’ command. Persistent.
[b]roguesymset[/b] — This option may be used to select one of the named symbol sets found within “symbols” to alter the symbols displayed on the screen on the rogue level.
[b]rlecomp[/b] — When writing out a save file, perform run length compression of the map. Not all ports support run length compression. It has no effect on reading an existing save file.

[b]runmode[/b] — Controls the amount of screen updating for the map window when engaged in multi-turn movement (running via shift+direction or control+direction and so forth, or via the travel command or mouse click). The possible values are:
[indent][b]teleport[/b] — update the map after movement has finished;[/indent]
[indent][b]run[/b] — update the map after every seven or so steps;[/indent]
[indent][b]walk[/b] — update the map after each step;[/indent]
[indent][b]crawl[/b] — like walk, but pause briefly after each step.[/indent]

This option only affects the game's screen display, not the actual results of moving. The default is “run”; versions prior to 3.4.1 used “teleport” only. Whether or not the effect is noticeable will depend upon the window port used or on the type of terminal. Persistent.
[b]safe_pet[/b] — Prevent you from (knowingly) attacking your pets (default on). Persistent.
[b]safe_wait[/b] — Prevents you from waiting or searching when next to a hostile monster (default on). Persistent.
[b]sanity_check[/b] — Evaluate monsters, objects, and map prior to each turn (default off). Debug mode only.

[b]scores[/b] — Control what parts of the score list you are shown at the end (for example “scores:5 top scores/4 around my score/own scores”). Only the first letter of each category (‘t’, ‘a’, or ‘o’) is necessary. Persistent.
[b]showdamage[/b] — Whenever your character takes damage, show a message of the damage taken, and the amount of hit points left.
[b]showexp[/b] — Show your accumulated experience points on bottom line (default off). Persistent.

[b]showrace[/b] — Display yourself as the glyph for your race, rather than the glyph for your role (default off). Note that this setting affects only the appearance of the display, not the way the game treats you. Persistent.
[b]showscore[/b] — Show your approximate accumulated score on bottom line (default off). By default, this feature is suppressed when building the program. Persistent.

[b]showvers[/b] — Include the game's version number on the status lines (default off). Potentially useful if you switch between different versions or variants, or you are making screenshots or streaming video. Using the [i]statuslines:3[/i] option is recommended so that there will be more room available for status information, unless you're using NetHack's [i]Qt[/i] interface or your terminal emulator window displays fewer than 25 lines. Persistent.
The [i]versinfo[/i] option provides limited control over what information [i]showvers[/i] displays.
[b]silent[/b] — Suppress terminal beeps (default on). Persistent.
[b]sortdiscoveries[/b] — Controls the sorting behavior for the output of the ‘[code]\[/code]’ and ‘[code]`[/code]’ commands. Persistent.
The possible values are:
[indent][b][code]o[/code][/b] — list object types by class, in discovery order within each class; default;[/indent]

[indent][b][code]s[/code][/b] — list object types by [i]sortloot[/i] classification: by class, by sub-class within class for classes which have substantial groupings (like helmets, boots, gloves, and so forth for armor), with object types partly-discovered via assigned name coming before fully identified types;[/indent]
[indent][b][code]c[/code][/b] — list by class, alphabetically within each class;[/indent]
[indent][b][code]a[/code][/b] — list alphabetically across all classes.[/indent]
Can be interactively set via the ‘[code]O[/code]’ command or via using the ‘[code]m[/code]’ prefix before the ‘[code]\[/code]’ or ‘[code]`[/code]’ command.
[b]sortloot[/b] — Controls the sorting behavior of the pickup lists for inventory and #loot commands and some others. Persistent.
The possible values are:
[indent][b]full[/b] — always sort the lists;[/indent]
[indent][b]loot[/b] — only sort the lists that don't use inventory letters, like with the #loot and pickup commands;[/indent]
[indent][b]none[/b] — show lists the traditional way without sorting; default.[/indent]
[b]sortpack[/b] — Sort the pack contents by type when displaying inventory (default on). Persistent.
[b]sortvanquished[/b] — Controls the sorting behavior for the output of the #vanquished command and also for the #genocided command. Persistent.
The possible values are:
[indent][b][code]t[/code][/b] — traditional—order by monster level; ties are broken by internal monster index; default;[/indent]
[indent][b][code]d[/code][/b] — order by monster difficulty rating; ties broken by internal index;[/indent]
[indent][b][code]a[/code][/b] — order alphabetically, first any unique monsters then all the others;[/indent]
[indent][b][code]c[/code][/b] — order by monster class, by low to high level within each class;[/indent]
[indent][b][code]n[/code][/b] — order by count, high to low; ties are broken by internal monster index;[/indent]
[indent][b][code]z[/code][/b] — order by count, low to high; ties broken by internal index.[/indent]
Can be interactively set via the ‘[code]m O[/code]’ command or via using the ‘[code]m[/code]’ prefix before either the #vanquished command or the #genocided command.
[b]sounds[/b] — Allow sounds to be emitted from an integrated sound library (default on).
[b]sparkle[/b] — Display a sparkly effect when a monster (including yourself) is hit by an attack to which it is resistant (default on). Persistent.
[b]spot_monsters[/b] — Show a message when hero notices a monster (default is off).
[b]standout[/b] — Boldface monsters and “[b]--More--[/b]” (default off). Persistent.

[b]statushilites[/b] — Controls how many turns status hilite behaviors highlight the field. If negated or set to zero, disables status hiliting. See “Configuring Status Hilites” for further information.
[b]status_updates[/b] — Allow updates to the status lines at the bottom of the screen (default true).

[b]suppress_alert[/b] — This option may be set to a NetHack version level to suppress alert notification messages about feature changes for that and prior versions (for example “suppress_alert:3.3.1”).

[b]symset[/b] — This option may be used to select one of the named symbol sets found within “symbols” to alter the symbols displayed on the screen. Use “symset:default” to explicitly select the default symbols.
[b]terrainstatus[/b] — Display an extra status condition describing the spot beneath the hero's feet (default off, not supported by all interfaces).
[b]time[/b] — Show the elapsed game time in turns on bottom line (default off). Persistent.

[b]timed_delay[/b] — When pausing momentarily for display effect, such as with explosions and moving objects, use a timer rather than sending extra characters to the screen. (Applies to “tty” and “curses” interfaces only; “X11” interface always uses a timer-based delay. The default is on if configured into the program.) Persistent.
[b]tips[/b] — Show some helpful tips during gameplay (default on). Persistent.
[b]tombstone[/b] — Draw a tombstone graphic upon your death (default on). Persistent.

[b]toptenwin[/b] — Put the ending display in a NetHack window instead of on stdout (default off). Setting this option makes the score list visible when a windowing version of NetHack is started without a parent window, but it no longer leaves the score list around after game end on a terminal or emulating window.

[b]travel[/b] — Allow the travel command via mouse click (default on). Turning this option off will prevent the game from attempting unintended moves if you make inadvertent mouse clicks on the map window. Does not affect traveling via the ‘[code]_[/code]’ (“#travel”) command. Persistent.
[b]tutorial[/b] — Play a tutorial level at the start of the game. Setting this option on or off in the config file will skip the query.
[b]verbose[/b] — Provide more commentary during the game (default on). Persistent.
[b]versinfo[/b] — Controls what the [i]showvers[/i] option displays on the status lines.
[b]weaponstatus[/b] — Display an extra status condition which describes currently wielded weapon (default off, not supported by all interfaces).
Some possible displayed values are:

[b]whatis_coord[/b] — When using the ‘/’ or ‘;’ commands to look around on the map with [i]autodescribe[/i] on, display coordinates after the description. Also works in other situations where you are asked to pick a location.
The possible settings are:
The [i]whatis_coord[/i] option is also used with the “/m”, “/M”, “/o”, and “/O” sub-commands of ‘/’, where the “none” setting is overridden with “map”.
[b]whatis_filter[/b] — When getting a location on the map, and using the keys to cycle through next and previous targets, allows filtering the possible targets.
The area-filter tries to be slightly predictive—if you're standing on a doorway, it will consider the area on the side of the door you were last moving towards.
Filtering can also be changed when getting a location with the “getpos.filter” key.
[b]whatis_menu[/b] — When getting a location on the map, and using a key to cycle through next and previous targets, use a menu instead to pick a target. (default off)

[b]whatis_moveskip[/b] — When getting a location on the map, and using shifted movement keys or meta-digit keys to fast-move, instead of moving 8 units at a time, move by skipping the same glyphs. (default off)

[b]windowtype[/b] — When the program has been built to support multiple interfaces, select which one to use, such as “tty” or “X11” (default depends on build-time settings; use “#version” to check). Cannot be set with the ‘[code]O[/code]’ command.

When used, it should be the first option set since its value might enable or disable the availability of various other options. For multiple lines in a configuration file, that would be the first non-comment line. For a comma-separated list in NETHACKOPTIONS or an OPTIONS line in a configuration file, that would be the [i]rightmost[/i] option in the list.
[b]wizweight[/b] — Augment object descriptions with their objects' weight (default off). Debug mode only.
[b]zerocomp[/b] — When writing out a save file, perform zero-comp compression of the contents. Not all ports support zero-comp compression. It has no effect on reading an existing save file.

chapters.title: Window Port Customization options
paragraphs: Here are explanations of the various options that are used to customize and change the characteristics of the windowtype that you have chosen. Character strings that are too long may be truncated. Not all window ports will adjust for all settings listed here. You can safely add any of these options to your configuration file, and if the window port is capable of adjusting to suit your preferences, it will attempt to do so. If it can't it will silently ignore it. You can find out if an option is supported by the window port that you are currently using by checking to see if it shows up in the Options list. Some options are dynamic and can be specified during the game with the ‘O’ command.
[b]align_message[/b] — Where to align or place the message window (top, bottom, left, or right)
[b]align_status[/b] — Where to align or place the status window (top, bottom, left, or right).

[b]ascii_map[/b] — If NetHack can, it should display the map using simple characters (letters and punctuation) rather than [i]tiles[/i] graphics. In some cases, characters can be augmented with line-drawing symbols; use the [i]symset[/i] option to select a symbol set such as [i]DECgraphics[/i] or [i]IBMgraphics[/i] if your display supports them. Setting [i]ascii_map[/i] to [i]True[/i] forces [i]tiled_map[/i] to be [i]False[/i].
[b]color[/b] — If NetHack can, it should display color if it can for different monsters, objects, and dungeon features (default on).
[b]eight_bit_tty[/b] — If NetHack can, it should pass eight-bit character values (for example, specified with the [i]traps[/i] option) straight through to your terminal (default off).
[b]font_map[/b] — if NetHack can, it should use a font by the chosen name for the map window.
[b]font_menu[/b] — If NetHack can, it should use a font by the chosen name for menu windows.
[b]font_message[/b] — If NetHack can, it should use a font by the chosen name for the message window.
[b]font_status[/b] — If NetHack can, it should use a font by the chosen name for the status window.
[b]font_text[/b] — If NetHack can, it should use a font by the chosen name for text windows.
[b]font_size_map[/b] — If NetHack can, it should use this size font for the map window.
[b]font_size_menu[/b] — If NetHack can, it should use this size font for menu windows.
[b]font_size_message[/b] — If NetHack can, it should use this size font for the message window.
[b]font_size_status[/b] — If NetHack can, it should use this size font for the status window.
[b]font_size_text[/b] — If NetHack can, it should use this size font for text windows.
[b]fullscreen[/b] — If NetHack can, it should try to display on the entire screen rather than in a window.
[b]guicolor[/b] — Use color text and/or highlighting attributes when displaying some non-map data (such as menu selector letters). Curses interface only; default is on.
[b]large_font[/b] — If NetHack can, it should use a large font.
[b]map_mode[/b] — If NetHack can, it should display the map in the manner specified.
[b]player_selection[/b] — If NetHack can, it should pop up dialog boxes, or use prompts for character selection.
[b]popup_dialog[/b] — If NetHack can, it should pop up dialog boxes for input.

[b]preload_tiles[/b] — If NetHack can, it should preload tiles into memory. For example, in the protected mode MS-DOS version, control whether tiles get pre-loaded into RAM at the start of the game. Doing so enhances performance of the tile graphics, but uses more memory. (default on). Cannot be set with the ‘[code]O[/code]’ command.
[b]scroll_amount[/b] — If NetHack can, it should scroll the display by this number of cells when the hero reaches the scroll_margin.
[b]scroll_margin[/b] — If NetHack can, it should scroll the display when the hero or cursor is this number of cells away from the edge of the window.
[b]selectsaved[/b] — If NetHack can, it should display a menu of existing saved games for the player to choose from at game startup, if it can. Not all ports support this option.
[b]softkeyboard[/b] — Display an onscreen keyboard. Handhelds are most likely to support this option.
[b]splash_screen[/b] — If NetHack can, it should display an opening splash screen when it starts up (default yes).
[b]statuslines[/b] — Number of lines for traditional below-the-map status display. Acceptable values are [code]2[/code] and [code]3[/code] (default is [code]2[/code]).

When set to [code]3[/code], the [code]tty[/code] interface moves some fields around and mainly shows status conditions on their own line. A display capable of showing at least 25 lines is recommended. The value can be toggled back and forth during the game with the ‘[code]O[/code]’ command.
The [code]curses[/code] interface does likewise if the [i]align_status[/i] option is set to [i]top[/i] or [i]bottom[/i] but ignores [i]statuslines[/i] when set to [i]left[/i] or [i]right[/i].

The [code]Qt[/code] interface already displays more than 3 lines for status so uses the [i]statuslines[/i] value differently. A value of [code]3[/code] renders status in the [code]Qt[/code] interface's original format, with the status window spread out vertically. A value of [code]2[/code] makes status be slightly condensed, moving some fields to different lines to eliminate one whole line, reducing the height needed. (If NetHack has been built using a version of [code]Qt[/code] older than [code]qt-5.9[/code], [i]statuslines[/i] can only be set in the run-time configuration file or via NETHACKOPTIONS, not during play with the ‘[code]O[/code]’ command.)
[b]term_cols [i]and[/i][/b] —

[b]term_rows[/b] — Curses interface only. Number of columns and rows to use for the display. Curses will attempt to resize to the values specified but will settle for smaller sizes if they are too big. Default is the current window size.
[b]tile_file[/b] — Specify the name of an alternative tile file to override the default.
Note: the X11 interface uses X resources rather than NetHack's options to select an alternate tile file. See [code]NetHack.ad[/code], the sample X “application defaults” file.
[b]tile_height[/b] — Specify the preferred height of each tile in a tile capable port.
[b]tile_width[/b] — Specify the preferred width of each tile in a tile capable port

[b]tiled_map[/b] — If NetHack can, it should display the map using [i]tiles[/i] graphics rather than simple characters (letters and punctuation, possibly augmented by line-drawing symbols). Setting [i]tiled_map[/i] to [i]True[/i] forces [i]ascii_map[/i] to be [i]False[/i].
[b]use_darkgray[/b] — Use bold black instead of blue for black glyphs (TTY only).
[b]use_inverse[/b] — If NetHack can, it should display inverse when the game specifies it.
[b]vary_msgcount[/b] — If NetHack can, it should display this number of messages at a time in the message window.
[b]windowborders[/b] — Whether to draw boxes around the map, status area, message area, and persistent inventory window if enabled. Curses interface only. Acceptable values are

(The 26x82 size threshold for ‘2’ refers to number of rows and columns of the display. A width of at least 110 columns (80+2+26+2) is needed to show borders if [i]align_status[/i] is set to [code]left[/code] or [code]right[/code].)

The persistent inventory window, when enabled, can grow until it is too big to fit on most displays, resulting in truncation of its contents. If borders are forced on (1) or the display is big enough to show them (2), setting the value to 3 or 4 instead will keep borders for the map, message, and status windows but have room for two additional lines of inventory plus widen each inventory line by two columns.
[b]windowcolors[/b] — If NetHack can, it should display all windows of a particular style with the specified foreground and background colors. Windows GUI and curses windowport only. The format is
[indent][b][code]OPTION=windowcolors:[/code][i]style foreground[/i][code]/[/code][i]background[/i][/b] —[/indent]

where [i]style[/i] is one of “menu”, “message”, “status”, or “text”, and [i]foreground[/i] and [i]background[/i] are colors, either numeric (hash sign followed by three pairs of hexadecimal digits, [i]#rrggbb[/i]), one of the named colors (black, red, green, brown, blue, magenta, cyan, orange, bright-green, yellow, bright-blue, bright-magenta, bright-cyan, white, gray, purple, silver, maroon, fuchsia, lime, olive, navy, teal, aqua), or (for Windows only) one of Windows UI colors (trueblack, activeborder, activecaption, appworkspace, background, btnface, btnshadow, btntext, captiontext, graytext, greytext, highlight, highlighttext, inactiveborder, inactivecaption, menu, menutext, scrollbar, window, windowframe, windowtext).
[b]wraptext[/b] — If NetHack can, it should wrap long lines of text if they don't fit in the visible area of the window.

chapters.title: Crash Report Options
paragraphs: Please note that NetHack does not send [b]any[/b] information off your computer unless you manually click submit on a form.
[indent][b]"OPTION=crash_email:[i]email_address[/i][/b] —[/indent]
[indent][b]"OPTION=crash_name:[i]your_name[/i][/b] —[/indent]
These options are used only to save you some typing on the crash report and #bugreport forms.
[indent][b]"OPTION=crash_urlmax:[i]bytes[/i][/b] —[/indent]
This option is used to limit the length of the URLs generated and is only needed if your browser cannot handle arbitrarily long URLs.

chapters.title: Platform-specific Customization options
paragraphs: Here are explanations of options that are used by specific platforms or ports to customize and change the port behavior.
[b]altkeyhandling[/b] — Select an alternate way to handle keystrokes (Win32 tty NetHack only). The name of the handling type is one of “default”, “ray”, “340”.

[b]altmeta[/b] — On systems where this option is available, it can be set to tell NetHack to convert a two character sequence beginning with ESC into a meta-shifted version of the second character (default off).

This conversion is only done for commands, not for other input prompts. Note that typing one or more digits as a count prefix prior to a command—preceded by [b]n[/b] if the [i]number_pad[/i] option is set—is also subject to this conversion, so attempting to abort the count by typing ESC will leave NetHack waiting for another character to complete the two character sequence. Type a second ESC to finish cancelling such a count. At other prompts a single ESC suffices.

[b]BIOS[/b] — Use BIOS calls to update the screen display quickly and to read the keyboard (allowing the use of arrow keys to move) on machines with an IBM PC compatible BIOS ROM (default off, OS/2, PC, and ST NetHack only).

[b]rawio[/b] — Force raw (non-cbreak) mode for faster output and more bulletproof input (MS-DOS sometimes treats ‘^P’ as a printer toggle without it) (default off, OS/2, PC, and ST NetHack only). Note: DEC Rainbows hang if this is turned on. Cannot be set with the ‘[code]O[/code]’ command.

[b]subkeyvalue[/b] — (Win32 tty NetHack only). May be used to alter the value of keystrokes that the operating system returns to NetHack to help compensate for international keyboard issues. OPTIONS=subkeyvalue:171/92 will return 92 to NetHack, if 171 was originally going to be returned. You can use multiple subkeyvalue assignments in the configuration file if needed. Cannot be set with the ‘[code]O[/code]’ command.

[b]video[/b] — Set the video mode used (PC NetHack only). Values are “autodetect”, “default”, “vga”, or “vesa”. Setting “vesa” will cause the game to display tiles, using the full capability of the VGA hardware. Setting “vga” will cause the game to display tiles, fixed at 640x480 in 16 colors, a mode that is compatible with all VGA hardware. Third party tilesets will probably not work. Setting “autodetect” attempts “vesa”, then “vga”, and finally sets “default” if neither of those modes works. Cannot be set with the ‘[code]O[/code]’ command.
[b]video_height[/b] — Set the VGA mode resolution height (MS-DOS only, with video:vesa)
[b]video_width[/b] — Set the VGA mode resolution width (MS-DOS only, with video:vesa)

[b]videocolors[/b] — Set the color palette for PC systems using NO_TERMS (default 4-2-6-1-5-3-15-12-10-14-9-13-11, (PC NetHack only). The order of colors is red, green, brown, blue, magenta, cyan, bright.white, bright.red, bright.green, yellow, bright.blue, bright.magenta, and bright.cyan. Cannot be set with the ‘[code]O[/code]’ command.

[b]videoshades[/b] — Set the intensity level of the three gray scales available (default dark normal light, PC NetHack only). If the game display is difficult to read, try adjusting these scales; if this does not correct the problem, try !color. Cannot be set with the ‘[code]O[/code]’ command.

chapters.title: Regular Expressions
paragraphs: Regular expressions are normally POSIX extended regular expressions. It is possible to compile NetHack without regular expression support on a platform where there is no regular expression library. While this is not true of any modern platform, if your NetHack was built this way, patterns are instead glob patterns; regardless, this document refers to both as ‘regular expressions.’ This applies to Autopickup exceptions, Message types, Menu colors, and User sounds.

chapters.title: Configuring Autopickup Exceptions
paragraphs: You can further refine the behavior of the [i]autopickup[/i] option beyond what is available through the [i]pickup_types[/i] option.
By placing [i]autopickup_exception[/i] lines in your configuration file, you can define patterns to be checked when the game is about to autopickup something.

[b]autopickup_exception[/b] — Sets an exception to the [i]pickup_types[/i] option. The [i]autopickup_exception[/i] option should be followed by a regular expression to be used as a pattern to match against the singular form of the description of an object at your location.
In addition, some characters are treated specially if they occur as the first character in the pattern, specifically:
The [i]autopickup_exception[/i] rules are processed in the order in which they appear in your configuration file, thus allowing a later rule to override an earlier rule.

Exceptions can be set with the ‘O’ command, but because they are not included in your configuration file, they won't be in effect if you save and then restore your game. [i]autopickup_exception[/i] rules and not saved with the game.
[b]Here are some examples:[/b] —

[code]autopickup_exception="<*arrow"
autopickup_exception=">*corpse"
autopickup_exception=">* cursed*"[/code]

The first example above will result in autopickup of any type of arrow. The second example results in the exclusion of any corpse from autopickup. The last example results in the exclusion of items known to be cursed from autopickup.

chapters.title: Changing Key Bindings
paragraphs: It is possible to change the default key bindings of some special commands, menu accelerator keys, and extended commands, by using BIND stanzas in the configuration file. Format is key, followed by the command to bind to, separated by a colon. The key can be a single character (“x”), a control key (“^X”, “C-x”), a meta key (“M-x”), a mouse button, or a three-digit decimal ASCII code.
For example:

[code]BIND=^X:getpos.autodescribe
BIND=\:menu_first_page
BIND=v:loot[/code]

[b]Extended command keys[/b] — You can bind multiple keys to the same extended command. Unbind a key by using “nothing” as the extended command to bind to. You can also bind the “<esc>”, “<enter>”, and “<space>” keys.

[b]Menu accelerator keys[/b] — The menu control or accelerator keys can also be rebound via OPTIONS lines in the configuration file. You cannot bind object symbols or selection letters into menu accelerators. Some interfaces only support some of the menu accelerators.
[b]Mouse buttons[/b] — You can bind “mouse1” or “mouse2” to “nothing”, “therecmdmenu”, “clicklook”, or “mouseaction”.

[b]Special command keys[/b] — Below are the special commands you can rebind. Some of them can be bound to same keys with no problems, others are in the same “context”, and if bound to same keys, only one of those commands will be available. Special command can only be bound to a single key.
[b]count[/b] — Prefix key to start a count, to repeat a command this many times. With [i]number_pad[/i] only. Default is ‘n’.
[b]getdir.help[/b] — When asked for a direction, the key to show the help. Default is ‘?’.

[b]getdir.mouse[/b] — When asked for a direction, the key to initiate a simulated mouse click. You will be asked to pick a location. Use movement keystrokes to move the cursor around the map, then type the getpos.pick.once key (default ‘[code],[/code]’) or the getpos.pick key (default ‘[code].[/code]’) to finish as if performing a left or right click. Only useful when using the [code]#therecmdmenu[/code] command. Default is ‘_’.
[b]getdir.self[/b] — When asked for a direction, the key to target yourself. Default is ‘.’.
[b]getdir.self2[/b] — When asked for a direction, an alternate key to target yourself. Default is ‘s’.
[b]getpos.autodescribe[/b] — When asked for a location, the key to toggle autodescribe. Default is ‘#’.
[b]getpos.all.next[/b] — When asked for a location, the key to go to next closest interesting thing. Default is ‘a’.
[b]getpos.all.prev[/b] — When asked for a location, the key to go to previous closest interesting thing. Default is ‘A’.
[b]getpos.door.next[/b] — When asked for a location, the key to go to next closest door or doorway. Default is ‘d’.
[b]getpos.door.prev[/b] — When asked for a location, the key to go to previous closest door or doorway. Default is ‘D’.
[b]getpos.help[/b] — When asked for a location, the key to show help. Default is ‘?’.
[b]getpos.mon.next[/b] — When asked for a location, the key to go to next closest monster. Default is ‘m’.
[b]getpos.mon.prev[/b] — When asked for a location, the key to go to previous closest monster. Default is ‘M’.
[b]getpos.obj.next[/b] — When asked for a location, the key to go to next closest object. Default is ‘o’.
[b]getpos.obj.prev[/b] — When asked for a location, the key to go to previous closest object. Default is ‘O’.
[b]getpos.menu[/b] — When asked for a location, and using one of the next or previous keys to cycle through targets, toggle showing a menu instead. Default is ‘!’.
[b]getpos.moveskip[/b] — When asked for a location, and using the shifted movement keys or meta-digit keys to fast-move around, move by skipping the same glyphs instead of by 8 units. Default is ‘*’.

[b]getpos.filter[/b] — When asked for a location, change the filtering mode when using one of the next or previous keys to cycle through targets. Toggles between no filtering, in view only, and in the same area only. Default is ‘"’.

[b]getpos.pick[/b] — When asked for a location, the key to choose the location, and possibly ask for more info. When simulating a mouse click after being asked for a direction (see getdir.mouse above), the key to use to respond as right click. Default is ‘.’.

[b]getpos.pick.once[/b] — When asked for a location, the key to choose the location, and skip asking for more info. When simulating a mouse click after being asked for a direction, the key to respond as left click. Default is ‘,’.
[b]getpos.pick.quick[/b] — When asked for a location, the key to choose the location, skip asking for more info, and exit the location asking loop. Default is ‘;’.
[b]getpos.pick.verbose[/b] — When asked for a location, the key to choose the location, and show more info without asking. Default is ‘:’.
[b]getpos.self[/b] — When asked for a location, the key to go to your location. Default is ‘@’.
[b]getpos.unexplored.next[/b] — When asked for a location, the key to go to next closest unexplored location. Default is ‘x’.
[b]getpos.unexplored.prev[/b] — When asked for a location, the key to go to previous closest unexplored location. Default is ‘X’.
[b]getpos.valid[/b] — When asked for a location, the key to go to show valid target locations. Default is ‘$’.
[b]getpos.valid.next[/b] — When asked for a location, the key to go to next closest valid location. Default is ‘z’.
[b]getpos.valid.prev[/b] — When asked for a location, the key to go to previous closest valid location. Default is ‘Z’.

chapters.title: Configuring Message Types
paragraphs: You can change the way the messages are shown in the message area, when the message matches a user-defined pattern.
In general, the configuration file entries to describe the message types look like this:
[indent]MSGTYPE=type "pattern"[/indent]
[indent][b]type[/b] — how the message should be shown;[/indent]
[indent][b]pattern[/b] — the pattern to match.[/indent]
The pattern should be a regular expression.
Allowed types are:
[indent][b]show[/b] — show message normally;[/indent]
[indent][b]hide[/b] — never show the message;[/indent]
[indent][b]stop[/b] — wait for user with more-prompt;[/indent]
[indent][b]norep[/b] — show the message once, but not again if no other message is shown in between.[/indent]
Here's an example of message types using NetHack's internal pattern matching facility:

[code]MSGTYPE=stop "You feel hungry."
MSGTYPE=hide "You displaced *."[/code]
specifies that whenever a message “You feel hungry” is shown, the user is prompted with more-prompt, and a message matching “You displaced <something>.” is not shown at all.
The order of the defined MSGTYPE lines is important; the last matching rule is used. Put the general case first, exceptions below them.

chapters.title: Configuring Menu Colors
paragraphs: Some platforms allow you to define colors used in menu lines when the line matches a user-defined pattern. At this time the tty, curses, win32tty and win32gui interfaces support this.
In general, the configuration file entries to describe the menu color mappings look like this:
[indent][b]MENUCOLOR="pattern"=color&attribute[/b] —[/indent]
[indent][b]pattern[/b] — the pattern to match;[/indent]
[indent][b]color[/b] — the color to use for lines matching the pattern;[/indent]

[indent][b]attribute[/b] — the attribute to use for lines matching the pattern. The attribute is optional, and if left out, you must also leave out the preceding ampersand. If no attribute is defined, no attribute is used.[/indent]
The pattern should be a regular expression.

Allowed colors are black, red, green, brown, blue, magenta, cyan, gray, orange, light-green, yellow, light-blue, light-magenta, light-cyan, and white. And [code]no-color[/code], the default foreground color, which isn't necessarily the same as any of the other colors.
Allowed attributes are none, bold, dim, italic, underline, blink, and inverse. “Normal” is a synonym for “none”. Note that the platform used may interpret the attributes any way it wants.
Here's an example of menu colors using NetHack's internal pattern matching facility:

[code]MENUCOLOR="* blessed *"=green
MENUCOLOR="* cursed *"=red
MENUCOLOR="* cursed *(being worn)"=red&underline[/code]

specifies that any menu line with “ blessed ” contained in it will be shown in green color, lines with “ cursed ” will be shown in red, and lines with “ cursed ” followed by “(being worn)” on the same line will be shown in red color and underlined. You can have multiple MENUCOLOR entries in your configuration file, and the last MENUCOLOR line that matches a menu line will be used for the line.

Note that if you intend to have one or more color specifications match “ uncursed ”, you will probably want to turn the [i]implicit_uncursed[/i] option off so that all items known to be uncursed are actually displayed with the “uncursed” description.

chapters.title: Configuring User Sounds
paragraphs: Some platforms allow you to define sound files to be played when a message that matches a user-defined pattern is delivered to the message window. At this time the Qt port and the win32tty and win32gui ports support the use of user sounds.
The following configuration file entries are relevant to mapping user sounds to messages:
[b]SOUNDDIR[/b] — The directory that houses the sound files to be played.
[b]SOUND[/b] — An entry that maps a sound file to a user-specified message pattern. Each SOUND entry is broken down into the following parts:
[indent][b]MESG[/b] — message window mapping (the only one supported in 5.0.0);[/indent]
[indent][b]msgtype[/b] — optional; message type to use, see “Configuring Message Types”[/indent]
[indent][b]pattern[/b] — the pattern to match;[/indent]
[indent][b]sound file[/b] — the sound file to play;[/indent]
[indent][b]volume[/b] — the volume to be set while playing the sound file;[/indent]
[indent][b]sound index[/b] — optional; the index corresponding to a sound file.[/indent]
The pattern should be a regular expression.
For example:

[code]SOUNDDIR=C:\nethack\sounds
SOUND=MESG "This door is locked" "lock.wav" 100
SOUND=MESG hide "^You miss the " "swing.wav" 75[/code]

chapters.title: Configuring Status Hilites
paragraphs: Your copy of NetHack may have been compiled with support for “Status Hilites”. If so, you can customize your game display by setting thresholds to change the color or appearance of fields in the status display.
The format for defining status colors is:
[code][code]OPTION=hilite_status:[/code][i]field-name[/i][code]/[/code][i]behavior[/i][code]/[/code][i]color[/i][code]&[/code][i]attributes[/i][code][/code][/code]
For example, the following line in your configuration file will cause the hitpoints field to display in the color red if your hitpoints drop to or below a threshold of 30%:
[code][code]OPTION=hilite_status:hitpoints/<=30%/red/normal[/code][/code]
(That example is actually specifying [code]red&normal[/code] for <=30% and [code]no-color&normal[/code] for >30%.)
For another example, the following line in your configuration file will cause wisdom to be displayed red if it drops and green if it rises:
[code][code]OPTION=hilite_status:wisdom/down/red/up/green[/code][/code]

Allowed colors are black, red, green, brown, blue, magenta, cyan, gray, orange, light-green, yellow, light-blue, light-magenta, light-cyan, and white. And “no-color”, the default foreground color on the display, which is not necessarily the same as black or white or any of the other colors.
Allowed attributes are none, bold, dim, underline, italic, blink, and inverse. “Normal” is a synonym for “none”; they should not be used in combination with any of the other attributes.
To specify both a color and an attribute, use ‘&’ to combine them. To specify multiple attributes, use ‘+’ to combine those. For example: “magenta&inverse+dim”.

Note that the display may substitute or ignore particular attributes depending upon its capabilities, and in general may interpret the attributes any way it wants. For example, on some display systems a request for bold might yield blink or vice versa. On others, issuing an attribute request while another is already set up will replace the earlier attribute rather than combine with it. Since NetHack issues attribute requests sequentially (at least with the [code]tty[/code] interface) rather than all at once, the only way a situation like that can be controlled is to specify just one attribute.
You can adjust the appearance of the following status fields:

[table=3][cell]title[/cell][cell]dungeon-level[/cell][cell]experience-level[/cell][cell]strength[/cell][cell]gold[/cell][cell]experience[/cell][cell]dexterity[/cell][cell]hitpoints[/cell][cell]HD[/cell][cell]constitution[/cell][cell]hitpoints-max[/cell][cell]time[/cell][cell]intelligence[/cell][cell]power[/cell][cell]hunger[/cell][cell]wisdom[/cell][cell]power-max[/cell][cell]carrying-capacity[/cell][cell]charisma[/cell][cell]armor-class[/cell][cell]condition[/cell][cell]alignment[/cell][cell][/cell][cell]score[/cell][/table]

The pseudo-field “characteristics” can be used to set all six of Str, Dex, Con, Int, Wis, and Cha at once. “HD” is “hit dice”, an approximation of experience level displayed when polymorphed. “experience”, “time”, and “score” are conditionally displayed depending upon your other option settings.

Instead of a behavior, “condition” takes the following condition flags: stone, slime, strngl, foodpois, termill, blind, deaf, stun, conf, hallu, lev, fly, and ride. You can use “major_troubles” as an alias for stone through termill, “minor_troubles” for blind through hallu, “movement” for lev, fly, and ride, and “all” for every condition.

Allowed behaviors are “always”, “up”, “down”, “changed”, a percentage or absolute number threshold, or text to match against. For the [i]hitpoints[/i] field, the additional behavior “criticalhp” is available. It overrides other behavior rules if hit points are at or below the [i]major problem[/i] threshold (which varies depending upon maximum hit points and experience level).
[indent][b]*[/b] — “always” will set the default attributes for that field.[/indent]
[indent][b]*[/b] — “up”, “down” set the field attributes for when the field value changes upwards or downwards. This attribute times out after [i]statushilites[/i] turns.[/indent]

[indent][b]*[/b] — “changed” sets the field attribute for when the field value changes. This attribute times out after [i]statushilites[/i] turns. (If a field has both a “changed” rule and an “up” or “down” rule which matches a change in the field's value, the “up” or “down” one takes precedence.)[/indent]

[indent][b]*[/b] — percentage sets the field attribute when the field value matches the percentage. It is specified as a number between 0 and 100, followed by ‘%’ (percent sign). If the percentage is prefixed with ‘<=’ or ‘>=’, it also matches when value is below or above the percentage. Use prefix ‘<’ or ‘>’ to match when strictly below or above. (The numeric limit is relaxed slightly for those: [code]>-1%[/code] and [code]<101%[/code] are allowed.) Only four fields support percentage rules. Percentages for “hitpoints” and “power” are straightforward; they're based on the corresponding maximum field. Percentage highlight rules are also allowed for “experience level” and “experience points” (valid when the [i]showexp[/i] option is enabled). For those, the percentage is based on the progress from the start of the current experience level to the start of the next level. So if level 2 starts at 20 points and level 3 starts at 40 points, having 30 points is 50% and 35 points is 75%. 100% is unattainable for experience because you'll gain a level and the calculations will be reset for that new level, but a rule for [code]=100%[/code] is allowed and matches the special case of being exactly 1 experience point short of the next level.[/indent]

[indent][b]*[/b] — absolute value sets the attribute when the field value matches that number. The number must be 0 or higher, except for “armor-class’ which allows negative values, and may optionally be preceded by ‘=’. If the number is preceded by ‘<=’ or ‘>=’ instead, it also matches when value is below or above. If the prefix is ‘<’ or ‘>’, only match when strictly above or below.[/indent]

[indent][b]*[/b] — criticalhp only applies to the hitpoints field and only when current hit points are below a threshold (which varies by maximum hit points and experience level). When the threshold is met, a criticalhp rule takes precedence over all other hitpoints rules.[/indent]

[indent][b]*[/b] — text match sets the attribute when the field value matches the text. Text matches can only be used for “alignment”, “carrying-capacity”, “hunger”, “dungeon-level”, and “title”. For title, only the role's rank title is tested; the character's name is ignored.[/indent]
The in-game options menu can help you determine the correct syntax for a configuration file.
The whole feature can be disabled by setting option [i]statushilites[/i] to 0.
Example hilites:

[code]OPTION=hilite_status: gold/up/yellow/down/brown
OPTION=hilite_status: characteristics/up/green/down/red
OPTION=hilite_status: hitpoints/100%/gray&normal
OPTION=hilite_status: hitpoints/<100%/green&normal
OPTION=hilite_status: hitpoints/<66%/yellow&normal
OPTION=hilite_status: hitpoints/<50%/orange&normal
OPTION=hilite_status: hitpoints/<33%/red&bold
OPTION=hilite_status: hitpoints/<15%/red&inverse
OPTION=hilite_status: condition/major/orange&inverse
OPTION=hilite_status: condition/lev+fly/red&inverse[/code]

chapters.title: Modifying NetHack Symbols
paragraphs: NetHack can load entire symbol sets from the symbol file.
The options that are used to select a particular symbol set from the symbol file are:
[b]symset[/b] — Set the name of the symbol set that you want to load.
[b]roguesymset[/b] — Set the name of the symbol set that you want to load for display on the rogue level.

You can also override one or more symbols using the SYMBOLS and ROGUESYMBOLS configuration file options. Symbols are specified as name:value pairs. Note that NetHack escape-processes the value string in conventional C fashion. This means that \ is a prefix to take the following character literally. Thus \ needs to be represented as \\.
